candidates.claim: rtr-01 has a MGMT-subnet interface (GigabitEthernet0, 10.10.99.12/24) with no ACL and a default route via 198.51.100.1 on the OUTSIDE interface, so MGMT traffic can be forwarded to OUTSIDE through rtr-01 without passing fw-01, because EDGE_IN is bound only inbound on Gi0/0/0 and does not filter that outbound direction.
candidates.remediation: Remove the rtr-01 default route via 10.10.99.1 and the MGMT-facing forwarding path, or filter MGMT traffic on rtr-01 so only the approved MGMT-to-NTP flow can leave the MGMT side.

candidates.claim: rtr-01 EDGE_IN permits any-source tcp/443 to 203.0.113.2, the fw-01 outside address, although the management policy allows HTTPS/ASDM only from MGMT on the fw-01 mgmt interface and fw-01 has its HTTP server enabled.
candidates.remediation: Remove the rtr-01 EDGE_IN entry at seq 40 unless a documented outside service needs it, and confirm no HTTPS management listener is reachable on the fw-01 outside interface.

clarifications.question: The management policy says IOS HTTP/HTTPS servers must be disabled, but fw-01 is an ASA with asa_http_server enabled (fw-01:109) and HTTP/ASDM management restricted to MGMT on the mgmt interface (fw-01:110). Is ASDM on fw-01 an approved management service under the policy, or should the ASA HTTP server be disabled?
